judgment.reason: Answer A contains fundamental conceptual errors: it incorrectly states that after drawing one red ball there are 3 balls remaining (should be 4) and after drawing one blue ball there is 1 red ball remaining (should be 3), leading to wrong conditional probabilities (2/3 and 1/2 instead of 2/4 and 1/4). Answer B correctly sets up the conditional probabilities as (3/5)*(2/4) and (2/5)*(1/4) but makes arithmetic errors, calculating 3/20 instead of 3/10 and 1/5 instead of 1/10. Both answers are incomplete (cut off by length), but B demonstrates correct understanding of the problem structure while A misunderstands the sample space.
